calls.prompt:
Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

Affected areas and owners:
- pharmacy-ops: Dispensing, controlled substances (DEA), pharmacist scope, vaccines → Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations)
- drug-safety: OTC products, labeling, recalls, shortages (FDA) → Daniel Brooks (Drug Safety & Quality)
- payers: Medicare Part D, Medicaid and insurer billing (CMS) → Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement)
- privacy-people: Patient privacy (HIPAA), records, store workforce → Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-10-23, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-10-23; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I found one document that qualifies. My searches couldn't pull the complete daily Federal Register lists for Oct 19–23, so other relevant documents may exist that I didn't find.

## Qualifying document

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Document number** | 2026-21420 |
| **Title** | Medicare Program; Implementation of Sections 6219, 6220, and 6224 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (CMS-4214-P) |
| **URL** | https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/20/2026-21420/medicare-program-implementation-of-sections-6219-6220-and-6224-of-the-consolidated-appropriations |
| **Published** | 2026-10-20, as a proposed rule |
| **Key deadline** | Comments are due by 5 p.m. Eastern on December 15, 2026. |
| **Tier** | **Critical.** It is a proposed rule, and the Dec 15 deadline is 53 days after 2026-10-23, which is under the 90-day cutoff. |
| **Owner area** | payers (Lucia Moreno, Reimbursement) |
| **Reason** | The rule would implement section 6219 (Part D cost-sharing reductions for low-income individuals) and section 6224 (pharmacy benefit manager accountability). It would also cut the generic copay from $1 to $0 for certain full-benefit dual-eligible enrollees, starting with plan years that begin January 1, 2028. CornerCare is a Part D pharmacy, so PBM payment rules and copay changes affect its reimbursement. The rule's rule of construction says nothing in the new remuneration section prohibits flat dispensing fees or payment for ingredient costs. |
| **Action** | Reimbursement should review the PBM remuneration and pharmacy-payment provisions, model the $0 generic copay impact on dual-eligible volume, and decide whether to file comments by Dec 15, 2026. |

## Reviewed and excluded

- **FDA guidance on prescription drug use-related software (2026-21516, Oct 21):** It applies to software outputs disseminated by or on behalf of a drug sponsor, so it is aimed at manufacturers.
- **FDA mandatory cosmetics recall Q&A (2026-21679, Oct 23), FDA information-collection notices (export certificates, product jurisdiction) and the patent-extension correction (2026-21711):** None of these concern pharmacy operations.
- **DEA decisions and orders (2026-21414, 2026-21410 on Oct 20; 2026-21725 and 2026-21799, filed Oct 23 and scheduled for Oct 26):** These are registration revocations of other registrants. They set no new requirement for CornerCare.
- **DEA bulk-manufacturer and importer applications (Oct 19):** These are manufacturer and importer matters.
- **HIPAA Privacy Rule final rule (2026-23429):** It was published November 19, 2026, so it falls outside the window. Privacy & HR Compliance (Sam Whitaker) should still track it.

I found nothing in the window from the CDC, the Department of Labor or Medicaid.

markdown:
# Regulatory triage — CornerCare Pharmacy
Window 2026-10-19 → 2026-10-23 · as of 2026-10-23 · 1 items

## Critical (1)

- **Medicare Program; Implementation of Sections 6219, 6220, and 6224 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026** [web search — verify]
  - Reimbursement (Lucia Moreno) should review the PBM remuneration and pharmacy-payment provisions, model the $0 generic copay impact on dual-eligible volume, and decide whether to file comments by Dec 15, 2026.
  - Dates: comment 2026-12-15 ✓ · Owner: Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement) · Areas: payers
  - 91 FR 66408 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/20/2026-21420/medicare-program-implementation-of-sections-6219-6220-and-6224-of-the-consolidated-appropriations

votes.why: Plain-English steps for Reimbursement that end in one concrete decision, whether to file comments by the deadline; 'PBM remuneration' is jargon but familiar to this owner.
The $0 generic copay for dual-eligibles and the PBM provisions match the reason; it neither calls the rule final nor says it sets pharmacy reimbursement or dispensing fees.
It conveys a proposed rule (comments invited) centered on PBM provisions, which adequately paraphrases the PBM accountability changes.
It names an owner but assigns three separate tasks and uses jargon such as “PBM remuneration.”
The reason supports reviewing PBM payment provisions and modeling the copay change, the comment deadline matches the verified date, and the action makes neither prohibited claim.
The action mentions PBM payment provisions but does not convey that the proposal would add accountability and transparency requirements for pharmacy benefit managers.
Plain-English instruction naming concrete review, modeling, and comment-decision steps for Lucia Moreno.
Claims the rule contains 'PBM remuneration and pharmacy-payment provisions,' which are not supported by the title, reason, or rubric.
Omits that these are Medicare Part D changes and fails to convey new accountability and transparency rules for PBMs.
